title: Structs against classes: value and reference semantics in practice

videos.script: Two keywords define a type of your own. Struct and class. They look almost the same on the page. {{kinds}} You will see the first difference before anything runs. A class asks you to write its initialiser, and a struct does not. {{copy}} Then the one that matters. Assign a struct, and you get a second value. Change it, and the first stays where it was. {{share}} Assign a class, and you get a second name for the same instance. Change it through either name, and both see it. {{mutating}} Then the word that makes let mean something for a struct. Mutating, on every method that changes the value. {{identity}} Equal, or the same one. Two operators for two questions. {{cow}} And the cost of all that copying, measured. An array shares its memory until somebody writes to it. {{choose}} By the end you can say which of the two the planner's data should be, and which the place that keeps it.
